statements.converted_sql:
SELECT 
    "businessentityid", 
    TO_CHAR("modifieddate", 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS') AS formattedmodifieddate, 
    DATE_PART('year', AGE(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, "birthdate")) AS age 
FROM bobsbookstore_dbo.author 
WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM "hiredate") = @HireDate;
statements.conversion_notes: Multiple SQL Server specific functions converted to PostgreSQL equivalents: FORMAT(date, format) -> TO_CHAR(date, format) with PostgreSQL format codes, DATEDIFF(YEAR, start, end) -> DATE_PART('year', AGE(end, start)), GETDATE() -> CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, DATEPART(YEAR, date) -> EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date). Column names changed to lowercase with quotes to handle PostgreSQL case sensitivity.
